candidate_result_row.claim: The knob set NUM_GAMES_PER_CYCLE 1000, NUM_THREADS_FOR_SHUFFLING 8, NUM_TRAIN_SAMPLES_PER_EPOCH 20000, MAX_TRAIN_PER_DATA 8, NUM_TRAIN_SAMPLES_PER_SWA 10000, BATCHSIZE 128, SHUFFLE_MINROWS 25000, MAX_TRAIN_SAMPLES_PER_CYCLE 100000, TAPER_WINDOW_SCALE 50000, SHUFFLE_KEEPROWS 120000, EPOCHS_PER_EXPORT 5 (passed as both -epochs-per-export and -max-epochs-this-instance), with --cpus-per-task 32 at numGameThreads 18, satisfies every constraint train.py and shuffle.py impose at the measured 9x9 rows/game, and does so at the 90 % lower bound of that measurement as well. Specifically: the per-cycle bucket gain games*r*reuse = 258400 (200620 at r_lo) exceeds 0.99*samples_per_epoch by 12.9x (10.0x) so training never starves (train.py:1256-1259,1434-1445); a cycle produces 32300 new rows (25078) against a 24000-row freshness floor of 1.2*samples_per_epoch; epochs_per_export = floor(min(gain, max(cap,E))/E) = 5 at both r and r_lo with a realised reuse of 3.10 (3.99) against the cap of 8; keep 120000 > cap 100000 (synchronous_loop.sh:66) and holds a whole cycle's 100000-sample draw; the shuffle window (shuffle.py:414-435 at -expand-window-per-row 0.4 -taper-window-exponent 0.65) holds at least one epoch in EVERY cycle including the first, worst case 195 batches against the 156 an epoch needs; the random bootstrap reaches min_rows in cycle 1 (31675 >= 25000, 28134 at r0_lo); swa_period = E//2 = 10000 is train.py:441's own default; the worst stage thread count 29 is inside the 32 declared; the projected cycle is 3.11 h so 23 whole cycles fit one 2-23:30:00 chain link; and the projection writes 16.11 MiB per cycle monotonic, 20.90 GiB after a full link against the 500 GiB cap in budget.env. TWO THINGS ARE NOT CLAIMED. (i) The knobs have never been executed -- no production cycle has run at them; the evidence is a derivation over measured inputs plus an executed arithmetic check, not a measurement of the loop at these values. (ii) 'Exactly one exported candidate per cycle' holds only from cycle 13. What holds from cycle 1 is AT MOST one, structurally, because -epochs-per-export equals -max-epochs-this-instance so train.py's persistent export_cycle_counter (:871,975,1743,1831) can advance by at most 5 per cycle; cycles 1-12 are window-limited to 1-4 epochs and the counter carries the remainder forward, so the export slips rather than duplicating. Forcing exactly one from cycle 1 would need SHUFFLE_MINROWS >= 100000 and hence >= 3554 random bootstrap games, which re-enters the NUM_GAMES derivation and diverges.

candidate_result_row._validator_decision_point: The two places to attack. (1) STATUS: is 'conditional' right, or is this 'symbolic derivation' with no empirical content at all? The inputs are measured and the output is an arithmetic consequence, so it is not a bare derivation, but nothing was measured at the derived point. (2) The K4 window model. It ports shuffle.py:414-435 verbatim and then applies min(window, keep) >= samples_per_epoch, which DELIBERATELY does not credit the file-granularity slack of shuffle.sh:48 (-approx-rows-per-out-file 70000). That makes K4 conservative -- and it is why the self-test reports the EXECUTED smoke as a K4 failure even though the smoke did export. A refuter should check that the conservatism runs in the safe direction everywhere it is used, and that the per-cycle usable-rows model (min_rows + (c-1)*games*r for c >= 2) is right about post-random rows being uncapped (shuffle.py:1073-1077).
